skills.name: Grid Systems
skills.summary: Column grids, gutters, and content max-widths: the alignment skeleton every layout composes on, from 12-col desktop to single-column mobile.

sections.definition: A grid system is the alignment contract of a layout: columns, gutters, and margins that every component snaps to. The web standard is a 12-column grid (divisible by 2, 3, 4, 6) with fluid gutters and a content max-width; mobile collapses to fewer columns or one. The grid is invisible when right - everything aligns for reasons users feel rather than see - and it is the substrate the other layout skills compose on.
principles: 12 columns on desktop, 8 on tablet, 4 on mobile: fewer columns as space shrinks; spans stay meaningful at every tier.
Gutters are tokens, not guesses: 16px mobile, 24px desktop from the spacing scale - gutters never invented per section.
Content max-width bounds reading: 1200-1440px on desktop; a 66ch reading measure inside it (typography guide 08).
Margins grow with viewport: edge padding scales (16/24/32/48px) so content never touches screen edges on large displays.
Components span columns, they do not define grids: sections consume grid classes; the grid definition is singular and global.
Grid alignment beats perfect symmetry: optical alignment (icons, text edges) may override mathematical edges - judge optically after building mathematically.
Breakpoint changes alter columns, not component anatomy: a card is the same card spanning 12 or 4 columns.

tokens.notes: App shell ceiling; reading content nested inside
Text content bound inside the grid
Native CSS Grid; no framework grid CSS

composition: Composes with css-grid-patterns and flexbox-patterns: the grid system is the vocabulary; those guides are its sentence patterns.
Composes with spacing tokens (skill-design-tokens guide 03): gutters and margins are spacing tokens - density modes re-map them once.
Composes with layout-compositions: sidebar, split, and bento layouts are named compositions of this grid.
patterns: Grid class vocabulary: .col-4/.col-6/.col-12 utilities generated from the token definition - one source, consistent spans.
Optical audit: after grid math, nudge optically (icon baselines, text edges) and document overrides - math first, eyes second.
useCases: App shells: sidebar + content grids for dashboards and admin tools.
Marketing pages: hero, feature, and footer sections snapping to one grid.
Audit: elements floating off-grid, gutter drift, margin chaos.
antiPatterns: Grid per section: every section redefining its own grid until nothing aligns across sections
Pixel-position layouts: absolute-positioned elements that shatter at any viewport change
Invisible gutters drift: 15px here, 18px there - alignment erodes one component at a time
Framework grid lock-in: Bootstrap columns overriding the token-defined grid

accessibility.notes: Grid alignment serves WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10: layouts that snap to tokens survive zoom and reflow; DOM order must follow visual column order (a11y repo keyboard-navigation).
accessibility.fallback: When a design cannot fit the grid, extend the grid via governance - never float an element off-grid as a one-off.

skills.name: Breakpoints Strategy
skills.summary: Content-driven breakpoints (not device names): a small tier set, mobile-first queries, and when container queries replace them.

sections.definition: Breakpoints are the viewport widths where layout reorganizes - and the strategy question is how few you can afford. Modern practice: mobile-first (base styles are the small-screen truth, min-width queries add complexity upward), 4-5 content-driven tiers (640/768/1024/1280/1536) named by what changes, never by devices (devices multiply; content is stable). Container queries (guide 03) are replacing page-level breakpoints for component-level adaptation.
principles: Mobile-first: base CSS is the mobile layout; min-width queries add columns and chrome as space allows.
Content defines breakpoints: add a tier when the design breaks, not when a new iPad ships - devices are an implementation detail.
Few tiers, named by change: 5 tiers maximum, each named for what reorganizes (nav-collapse, sidebar-reveal, 3-col).
One unit system per concern: px for viewport queries, em for component queries (respects user font size).
Every tier is tested: layouts are signed off at each tier's width, not just desktop and 'roughly mobile'.
No breakpoint inside components that own a container: components with container queries ignore viewport tiers - one owner per adaptation.
Ranges never overlap: min-width chains exclusive (max-width: 767.98px patterns die; single-axis min-width stacks).

tokens.notes: Base = mobile; queries add complexity upward
Wide desktop; content max-width governs beyond
Container queries size in em (user-font aware)
Components adapt via container queries; page tiers only for shell

composition: Composes with grid-systems: tiers change grid column counts and margins - the grid is the thing being reorganized.
Composes with fluid-container-queries: the strategy decides what adapts at page level vs container level; overlap is the failure mode.
Composes with mobile-navigation (guide 08): nav collapse is the most common breakpoint-driven change.
patterns: Tier-per-change map: a table of tiers x what changes (columns, nav, sidebar, density) reviewed before building - unowned tiers get deleted.
min-width stack: one-directional media queries layered in source order; no max-width unless a legacy base demands it.
useCases: App shells with responsive sidebars and nav.
Marketing pages with tiered section layouts.
Audit: dead breakpoints, device-named tiers, overlapping ranges.
antiPatterns: Device-named tiers: iPad-Pro-2 breakpoints that multiply every product cycle
Breakpoint soup: 14 overlapping queries nobody dares delete
Desktop-first shrink: max-width overrides fighting the base layout instead of mobile-first growth
Untested tiers: layouts signed off at 1440px and broken at 1024px where half the users are

accessibility.notes: Breakpoints must preserve WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10: zoom to 400% reflows to the single-column tier - test at zoom widths, not just device widths; em-based component queries respect user font size.
accessibility.fallback: If a tier cannot be tested in time, degrade to the nearest tested tier and ship the gap as a documented known issue - never an untested silent tier.

skills.name: Fluid Layout & Container Queries
skills.summary: Components that adapt to their container, not the viewport: container queries, cqi units, and fluid spacing/type between bounds.

sections.definition: Container queries invert responsive design: instead of components asking 'how wide is the viewport', they ask 'how wide is my container' - so a card renders its compact variant in a sidebar and its full variant in the main column, with no viewport knowledge. Combined with fluid spacing/type (clamp on cqi units) and intrinsic sizing (min/max-content), layouts become truly reusable: the same component works anywhere it is dropped.
principles: Container queries for components, media queries for the shell: page chrome (nav, sidebar reveal) stays viewport-driven; widgets adapt to their slot.
Name containers by role: .card-container, .widget-container - containment is explicit, never accidental global containment.
cqi/cqw for internal fluid sizing: container query units make internal type/spacing scale with the container, not the screen.
Every container-queried component has 2-3 named states: compact / standard / expanded - states documented like the breakpoints they replaced.
Fallbacks for legacy browsers: modern targets are fine (container queries are Baseline 2023), but feature-detect rather than assume in long-support products.
Fluid bounds are tokens: clamp() endpoints come from the spacing/type scales - fluidity never introduces off-scale values.
Test components in their narrowest slot: a card tested only full-width will break in the sidebar it was promised to work in.

tokens.notes: Widgets adapt to containers; shell uses media queries
Default containment; height queries are rare
Widget title scales in container space
Every container component tested in its 3 slots

composition: Composes with grid-systems and layout-compositions: containers are the slots the grid creates; components adapt inside them.
Composes with breakpoints-strategy: the strategy split (shell vs component) prevents double adaptation - one owner per responsive decision.
Composes with typography fluid tokens (skill-typography guide 06): cqi-based type inside containers follows the same clamp discipline.
patterns: Slot-tested components: each container-aware component ships with a test page rendering it in sidebar/main/modal slots simultaneously.
Progressive containment: add container-type to wrappers; components declare @container rules that no-op gracefully without a named ancestor.
useCases: Design systems: one card component that works in every slot.
Dashboard widgets rearranged per user (masonry/bento).
CMS-driven pages where component placement is unpredictable.
antiPatterns: Double adaptation: a component with both media and container queries fighting over the same decision
Anonymous containment: container-type sprinkled globally, changing layout for everything downstream
Viewport-brained components: widgets that ask viewport width and break in sidebars
Untested narrow slots: container components shipped after testing only full-width

accessibility.notes: Container adaptation must keep WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10 floors: compact states never shrink text below 12px or targets below 24px - adapt the layout, not the legibility.
accessibility.fallback: If container queries are unsupported in a required target, the feature-detect fallback renders the standard (viewport-based) variant - compact variants are progressive enhancement.

skills.name: Flexbox Patterns
skills.summary: One-dimensional layout patterns: nav bars, media objects, toolbars, and the alignment/gap idioms that solve 80% of component layout.

sections.definition: Flexbox solves one-dimensional layout: rows and columns of items that distribute space, align, and wrap. Its patterns cover most component-level layout - nav bars, media objects, button groups, toolbars, form rows - with gap, align-items, and flex shorthand as the core vocabulary. The skill is knowing when flex is wrong: two-dimensional layouts belong to CSS Grid (guide 05), and content-flow documents belong to normal flow.
principles: One axis = flexbox: toolbars, nav rows, button groups, media objects - if items flow in one direction, flex is the tool.
Two dimensions = grid: page scaffolding and card grids belong to CSS Grid; forcing flex grids creates wrapper-div soup.
gap over margins: flex gap handles spacing without :last-child overrides and works with wrap.
flex: 1 is 'fill remaining', not 'equal': flex-grow distributes leftover space; min-width: 0 is required for content to shrink (the classic overflow bug).
align-items for cross-axis truth: center alignment of mixed-height content (icon + two-line text) is flex's killer feature.
wrap is a layout decision: flex-wrap on toolbars that must reflow; nowrap with overflow handling on scrollable rails.
Respect intrinsic content: flex items size to content first - forcing equal widths needs flex-basis or grid, not min-width hacks.

tokens.notes: Nav bars: logo left, actions right, centered items
Icon/avatar + content rows; the workhorse pattern
Horizontal card rails; pairs with scroll-animation

composition: Composes with css-grid-patterns: grid lays the page, flex lays the components inside grid areas - the standard two-layer architecture.
Composes with spacing tokens: gap values are space tokens; density modes tighten gaps once at the token tier.
Composes with rtl-i18n-layout: flex follows direction automatically (row-reverse not needed) - logical properties keep RTL free.
patterns: Media-object everywhere: avatar/icon + text rows (comments, list items, notifications) as one shared pattern class.
Toolbar contract: action bars use flex-wrap + gap so overflow reflows instead of clipping; overflow rails are a named exception.
useCases: Component-level layout inside grid areas: cards, list items, form rows.
App shell header/footer with sticky-footer pattern.
Horizontal scroll rails for card carousels.
antiPatterns: Flex-as-grid: nesting three wrapper divs to fake two-dimensional layout that grid expresses in one rule
Shrink-less overflow: flex children without min-width: 0 pushing parents wider than the screen
Margin-based spacing: :last-child margin overrides instead of gap
Infinite nowrap: toolbars that clip actions instead of wrapping

accessibility.notes: Flex order is visual order: never use order/row-reverse to fix visual sequence at the cost of DOM/tab order mismatch (a11y repo 2.4.3) - reorder the DOM.
accessibility.fallback: If a flex pattern cannot preserve DOM=visual order, restructure the markup; visual-only reordering of interactive elements is a blocker.

skills.name: CSS Grid Patterns
skills.summary: Two-dimensional layout: page shells, card grids with auto-fit, named areas, and subgrid - the patterns that replaced framework grids.

sections.definition: CSS Grid is two-dimensional layout: rows and columns designed together. Its patterns cover page scaffolding (header/main/sidebar/footer in one rule), responsive card grids (auto-fill/auto-fit with minmax), named template areas that make layout readable, and subgrid for aligning nested content. Grid made framework grid systems optional - the native primitives are more capable and token-friendly.
principles: Grid for the page skeleton: header/main/aside/footer in one grid-template-areas rule - readable, reorderable per breakpoint.
auto-fill + minmax for card grids: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr)) responds to available space without breakpoints.
Named areas are documentation: grid-template-areas strings read like layout diagrams - prefer them over numbered lines.
minmax() encodes constraints: minimum comfortable card width + maximum stretch in one declaration.
Subgrid aligns nested rhythm: card internals (title/meta rows) align across a grid row with subgrid.
gap consumes space tokens: grid gap is the 4px scale - gutters stay consistent with the rest of the system.
Implicit grid is a smell: auto-placed items are fine, but important placements get explicit areas - debuggable and RTL-safe.

tokens.notes: App shell in one template-areas rule
Until masonry ships: columns() or JS masonry

composition: Composes with grid-systems: the 12-col system can be implemented AS a CSS grid pattern; named areas implement the compositions.
Composes with flexbox-patterns: grid areas hold flex components - the two-layer rule that keeps both readable.
Composes with layout-compositions: bento, split, and sidebar layouts are named grid-template-areas strings.
patterns: Area-string breakpoints: layout reorganization expressed by swapping grid-template-areas per tier - the whole page change in 3 lines.
minmax card catalog: the design system documents its minmax presets (card 240px, table 480px, widget 320px) once.
useCases: App shells and dashboard scaffolding.
Responsive card/product grids without breakpoints.
Bento/marketing grids with mixed-size cells.
antiPatterns: 12-wrapper-col markup: framework-style div.col-md-6 wrappers instead of native minmax/auto-fill
Magic line numbers: grid-column: 3 / 7 scattered without named lines or areas
Fixed-height rows: hardcoded row heights that break with dynamic content
Grid-inside-grid confusion: subgrid ignored where nested alignment was the actual goal

accessibility.notes: Grid reordering must keep DOM order aligned with visual reading order (a11y 1.3.2/2.4.3): template-areas reorganization is visual only - the source order stays logical; grid-dense packing must not create confusing tab sequences.
accessibility.fallback: If a grid pattern reorders interactive elements visually, restructure the DOM to match - visual-only reordering of focusable content is a blocker.

skills.name: Named Layout Compositions
skills.summary: The catalog: sidebar, split, stack, cluster, bento, holy-grail - named, token-driven compositions instead of re-solved layout problems.

sections.definition: Layout compositions are named solutions to recurring layout problems: the sidebar+main shell, the split-pane, the stack (vertical rhythm), the cluster (wrapped chips), the bento grid, the holy grail. Giving them names and token-driven implementations turns layout from per-page problem-solving into a catalog - designers and engineers say 'split with 320px sidebar' and both know exactly what renders.
principles: Name every reusable layout: unnamed layouts cannot be reused or audited - the catalog is the API.
Compositions consume tokens: sidebar widths, gaps, and max-widths are tokens - a composition has no magic numbers.
Each composition declares its responsive behavior: how it collapses (sidebar -> drawer, split -> stack) is part of the name's contract.
Stack is the default; complexity is earned: most content is a stack with gaps - reach for sidebar/split only when hierarchy demands it.
Bento grids need hierarchy rules: mixed-size cells must follow a size grammar (1 large + 2 medium + n small), not random tiles.
Compositions nest predictably: sidebar contains stacks and clusters; nesting is documented, depth-capped (3 levels).
Every composition is RTL-safe and container-aware: logical properties + container queries are baked into the catalog, not added per use.

tokens.notes: Sidebar + fluid main; collapses to drawer under lg
Equal split panes; stacks under md
The catalog lives in the DS; pages consume it

composition: Compositions are the consuming layer of grid-systems, flexbox-patterns, and css-grid-patterns - the patterns become named products.
Composes with fluid-container-queries: compositions declare container-type so nested components adapt per slot.
Composes with skill-component-recipes: component recipes assume the catalog (tables render inside 'sidebar' or 'split' compositions).
patterns: Catalog-as-code: each composition is a small class/utility with token inputs and documented collapse behavior - pages compose them.
Collapse-contract table: one table listing every composition x its mobile behavior; new compositions fill a row before shipping.
useCases: Design systems shipping layout primitives (Radix/Every Layout style).
Rapid page assembly from named layouts instead of bespoke CSS.
Audit: pages re-implementing 'sidebar' badly instead of consuming the composition.
antiPatterns: Bespoke everything: every page re-solving sidebar layout with different values
Magic-number compositions: named layouts with hardcoded px inside
Undeclared collapse: compositions whose mobile behavior is discovered in QA
Nesting spirals: 6-deep composition stacks where 2 would do

accessibility.notes: Composition collapse behavior is an accessibility surface: sidebar->drawer must preserve focus management and DOM order (a11y repo guides 03/04); collapse must never hide content from AT without disclosure.
accessibility.fallback: If a composition cannot collapse accessibly (e.g. bento on mobile), it stacks in DOM order - visual bento is a wide-screen enhancement only.

skills.name: Responsive Images & Media
skills.summary: srcset/sizes, art direction, modern formats, and lazy loading: images that ship the right bytes for every slot and bandwidth.

sections.definition: Images dominate page weight; responsive image technique ships the right pixels for the slot: srcset/sizes for resolution switching, <picture> for art direction (different crops per viewport), AVIF/WebP with fallbacks, lazy loading below the fold, and aspect-ratio boxes that reserve space (zero CLS). The skill is treating images as layout citizens - sized by tokens, loaded strategically, never causing shift.
principles: srcset + sizes for the common case: let the browser pick from a width descriptor list; sizes must match the actual rendered slot.
Art direction via <picture> only when crops differ: mobile hero needs a different crop - that is picture; mere resizing is srcset.
AVIF first, WebP fallback: modern formats cut 30-50% of JPEG weight; the type attribute negotiates per browser.
Lazy-load below the fold: loading=lazy on non-critical images; above-the-fold stays eager + preload for LCP.
Aspect-ratio boxes kill CLS: width/height or aspect-ratio on every img - space reserved before bytes arrive.
Object-fit for slot-filling: cover/contain semantics explicit - never distort; focal point via object-position for crops.
LCP image is special: preload it, fetchpriority=high, no lazy - the largest contentful paint drives perceived speed.
Alt text is part of the image contract: every meaningful image ships with alt (a11y repo media-alt-text).

tokens.notes: sizes attr mirrors the layout's real slot width
Different crops per viewport; not mere resizing
loading=lazy below fold; eager + preload for LCP
Fluid base: images never overflow containers

composition: Composes with layout compositions: slot sizes (sidebar, card, hero) generate the sizes attribute values - layout informs loading.
Composes with perceived-performance (skill-design-review guide 10): LCP/CLS from images are the top perceptual-speed factors.
Composes with skill-animation scroll-animation: parallax/lazy-reveal images follow the same loading discipline.
patterns: Image component with slots: one <Image> wrapper consuming slot tokens (card/hero/sidebar) and emitting correct srcset/sizes/lazy/preload.
Zero-CLS rule: CI checks every img for explicit dimensions/aspect-ratio; a shift-causing image fails the build.
useCases: E-commerce grids: hundreds of product images sized right per card.
Editorial/hero pages with art-direction crops.
Perf audits: LCP, CLS, wasted bytes from oversized images.
antiPatterns: Desktop images everywhere: 2000w hero rendered in a 300px slot
CLS by images: no dimensions on img - the whole page jumps on load
Lazy LCP: loading=lazy on the hero image, tanking the largest paint
Distorted fills: stretched thumbnails from missing object-fit

accessibility.notes: Every informative image carries alt (a11y repo guide 09); decorative images alt='' - and aspect-ratio reservation prevents the layout jumps that disorient zoom and screen-magnifier users.
accessibility.fallback: If art direction cannot be produced per viewport, ship one well-cropped 16:9 master with object-fit - a single good crop beats three bad ones.

skills.name: Mobile Navigation
skills.summary: Bottom bars, drawers, and the thumb zone: navigation patterns that work at 360px with one thumb - and when to collapse what.

sections.definition: Mobile navigation reorganizes for a 360px viewport and a thumb-reachable zone: top bars shrink to logo + actions, primary destinations move to a bottom bar (3-5 items), everything else tucks into drawers or full-screen menus. The craft is deciding what earns a bottom-bar slot, what collapses, and how the drawer preserves focus and context (a11y repo guides 03/04).
principles: 3-5 items in the bottom bar: thumb-reachable, icon + label, current item visually and semantically marked (aria-current).
Thumb zone rules: primary actions bottom-right for right-handed reach; destructive actions away from the thumb's resting arc.
Top bar shrinks, never stacks: 56px max; logo + title + one-two actions; everything else moves down.
Drawers and sheets for secondary nav: slide-in panels with focus trap, Escape/scrim close, and focus return (dialog contract).
Menus collapse by importance, not alphabet: the nav audit ranks destinations by frequency; the cut line is data-driven.
Breadcrumb or back over deep menus: mobile hierarchy favors back-stack and breadcrumbs over mega-menus.
44px targets everywhere: nav items meet the touch floor; icon-only items get labels or aria-label (a11y repo 2.5.8).

tokens.notes: Bottom bar icons carry labels (recognition over recall)
Cut line from analytics, not alphabet

composition: Composes with breakpoints-strategy: nav collapse is the lg-tier change (bottom bar appears, sidebar becomes drawer).
Composes with layout-compositions: the shell composition declares its mobile nav contract (which comp collapses to what).
Composes with a11y focus-management: drawers implement the trap-and-return dialog contract exactly.
patterns: Bottom-bar + drawer stack: primary destinations in the bar, the long tail in a 'More' sheet - the standard mobile IA.
Nav-collapse contract: the layout catalog documents where each nav tier lives (desktop sidebar / tablet drawer / mobile bar+sheet).
useCases: Responsive web apps adapting desktop IA to mobile.
PWA/mobile-first products designing thumb-first from the start.
Audit: unlabeled icon nav, unreachable menus, trap-less drawers.
antiPatterns: Hamburger everything: all navigation hidden behind one icon - discovery dies
Icon-only bottom bars: unlabeled glyphs users must memorize
Top-bar overflow: 8 actions crammed into a 56px bar
Trap-less drawers: slide-ins without focus management or Escape

accessibility.notes: Mobile nav is an a11y hotspot: bottom-bar items need aria-current + labels, drawers need the full dialog contract (trap, Escape, return), and 44px targets (2.5.8) are the floor - see a11y repo guides 03/04/06.
accessibility.fallback: If drawer focus management cannot be built in time, use a full-page menu (normal document flow, no trap) - simpler and accessible by default.

skills.name: Responsive Data Tables
skills.summary: Tables that survive narrow screens: priority columns, card fallback, sticky headers, and horizontal scroll done honestly.

sections.definition: Data tables are the hardest responsive problem: they are dense, two-dimensional, and comparison-oriented - exactly what small screens hate. The strategy ladder: (1) reduce columns by priority, (2) allow honest horizontal scroll with sticky first column, (3) restructure to stacked cards per row as last resort (losing comparability). The choice is per-table by data type - and horizontal scroll with sticky headers beats pseudo-card tables for comparison tasks.
principles: Cut before you adapt: mobile tables show priority columns (2-4); the rest live in a detail view - column priority is an IA decision.
Horizontal scroll is honest: a scrollable table with sticky header + sticky identifier column preserves comparability; hide-scroll-by-crop is a lie.
Card-stack is the last resort: stacked rows lose column comparison - use only when rows are self-contained records (orders, messages).
Sticky first column = row identity: the identifier column pins so users never lose which row they are reading.
Row height and touch targets: 48px rows; row actions as a menu, not a hover-only toolbar (hover does not exist on touch).
Numeric columns stay tabular: tnum figures + right alignment (typography guide 10) - alignment survives adaptation.
Scroll indicators are visible: a faded edge or shadow marks truncation; users must know more exists (3.2.x predictability).

tokens.notes: IA decision: which columns survive mobile
Default adaptation: honest scroll, pinned identity
Column headers persist on vertical scroll
Card stacking only for record-like rows
Row actions in a kebab menu on touch
Tables never compress below readable column width
Sort headers meet the touch floor

composition: Composes with grid-systems: tables span the full content column; their scroll container respects the shell's margins.
Composes with skill-component-recipes guide 03 (tables): the recipe owns features (sort/filter/pagination); this guide owns responsive behavior.
Composes with numeric-tabular (skill-typography guide 10): alignment and figure style are shared contracts.
patterns: Priority-column matrix: per table, document columns x importance (mobile/core/extended); the mobile set falls out of the matrix.
Sticky-scroll pattern: scroll container + position-sticky th + sticky first column + edge fade - the reusable honest-scroll implementation.
useCases: Admin/enterprise tools where tables are the primary surface.
Finance and analytics products with comparison-critical tables.
Audit: hover-only actions, cropped scroll, card-tables that lost comparability.
antiPatterns: Crop-scroll lie: tables that silently clip columns with no scroll affordance
Card-table everything: comparison data stacked into cards, destroying the only reason it was a table
Hover-only row actions: toolbars invisible to touch and keyboard users
Squeezed columns: letting tables compress until cells wrap into unreadable slivers

accessibility.notes: Tables need real <table> semantics (th scope, caption) regardless of visual adaptation (a11y repo aria-fundamentals); scroll containers must stay keyboard-scrollable and actions keyboard-reachable (2.1.1).
accessibility.fallback: If the card fallback is used, keep a 'switch to table view' control - comparability is user-selectable, not design-fated.

skills.name: Intrinsic Layout
skills.summary: Layouts from content, not viewport: min/max/clamp sizing, aspect-ratio, and the Every-Layout approach that needs fewer breakpoints.

sections.definition: Intrinsic design builds layouts from the content's own size preferences instead of viewport assumptions: min-content, max-content, fit-content, clamp(), and aspect-ratio let components absorb available space gracefully across any width. Popularized by Every Layout, the approach produces layouts that need dramatically fewer media queries - the content flexes, the viewport merely bounds it. It is the philosophy behind why modern CSS needs fewer breakpoints, not more.
principles: Sizing from content: min-content and max-content describe what content needs; layout math starts there, not from a guessed px value.
clamp() is the workhorse: min 0, ideal some fraction, max 1 - the sidebar pattern minmax(auto, 1fr) absorbs space without queries.
The 'sidebar' pattern needs no breakpoint: grid-template-columns: fit-content(280px) 1fr collapses naturally as space shrinks.
aspect-ratio reserves space declaratively: media boxes and cards hold their shape without padding hacks.
Fewer queries is a symptom of good intrinsic math: if every component needs 3 queries, the sizing strategy is wrong.
Intrinsic + container queries compose: intrinsic sizing decides how a component wants to flex; container queries decide which variant renders.
Intrinsic does not mean uncontrolled: max-width tokens and ch measures still bound growth - content-flexing within documented limits.

tokens.notes: The floor a flex item may shrink to
Reading measure as an intrinsic bound
Columns that absorb space, never overflow
Media queries added when content, not viewport, demands
Continuous resize test, no fixed tier set

composition: Composes with fluid-container-queries: intrinsic sizing is the pre-CQ philosophy; together they cover 'how it flexes' and 'which variant renders'.

Caution with grid-systems and breakpoints-strategy: fixed 12-col tiers and fixed tier sets answer a different question - document which approach owns each surface instead of mixing both in one component.
Composes with responsive-images: aspect-ratio and intrinsic width are shared contracts between layout and media.
patterns: The Every Layout primitives: stack, cluster, sidebar, switcher, center, cover, grid - implemented once as reusable, query-light classes.
Query-budget audit: count media/container queries per component; more than 1-2 signals the intrinsic math should be redone.
useCases: Content-of-unknown-length surfaces: CMS pages, i18n text, user-generated content.
Component libraries meant to work in any slot without slot knowledge.
Refactors reducing breakpoint count without losing responsive quality.
antiPatterns: Viewport-brained defaults: fixed widths everywhere with queries papering over the cracks
Query inflation: 4 queries per component because the sizing strategy was never intrinsic
Unbounded flexing: intrinsic sizing with no max-width tokens - text lines run to 200ch on wide screens
Cargo-cult minimalism: refusing any breakpoint where a genuine content break exists

accessibility.notes: Intrinsic sizing is a zoom/accessibility ally: content-driven layouts survive 200%-400% zoom and text-spacing overrides better than fixed-width ones (WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10) - flexing content IS the reflow strategy.
accessibility.fallback: Where intrinsic patterns cannot express a required design, add the minimal named breakpoint and document it - pragmatism over dogma.

skills.name: RTL & i18n Layout
skills.summary: Layouts that flip, reflow, and re-text for every locale: logical properties, RTL mirroring, text expansion, and internationalization-safe responsive design.

sections.definition: An internationalized layout survives translation: Arabic/Hebrew flip it horizontally (RTL), German lengthens labels by 35%, Thai changes line-breaking rules, and CJK changes both reading and type expectations. The modern toolkit makes this cheap: CSS logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, inset-inline) replace physical directions, flex/grid follow direction automatically, and text expansion budgets are planned in component design - so localization becomes configuration, not a layout rewrite.
principles: Logical properties everywhere: margin-inline-start, not margin-left; padding-block, not padding-top - direction becomes a single dir attribute flip.
Flex and grid are direction-aware: row follows writing direction; row-reverse to 'fix' RTL is a bug, not a fix.
Plan for 30-40% text expansion: German/Finnish labels grow; buttons, nav items, and table headers need flexible widths, never fixed.
Mirroring is semantic, not absolute: media players, progress bars, and timelines flip direction; logos, media controls for playback, and clock faces do not.
dir attribute is set at the html level and corrected per-fragment: user-generated RTL content inside LTR pages gets dir=auto.
Icons and arrows flip when directional: back arrows, chevrons, and indent icons mirror; brand marks and checkmarks do not.
Test the full locale matrix: one RTL locale (Arabic), one long-word locale (German), one CJK (Japanese) - the minimum QA set.

Labels/UI strings sized to survive German-length translations
Which icons/glyphs flip in RTL; the rest never do
No row-reverse hacks; direction flows from dir
Minimum QA locale set: RTL + long-word + CJK
Date/number formatting via Intl, never hand-rolled
Sidebar/logo/actions mirror; content order stays DOM order
Arabic/CJK/Thai faces in the fallback chain where needed

composition: Composes with grid-systems and layout-compositions: the shell's mirroring contract (what flips, what does not) is documented per composition.
Composes with flexbox-patterns: flex follows direction automatically - patterns here must never hardcode physical directions.
Composes with multilingual-vietnamese (skill-typography guide 07): script coverage and fallback stacks are shared contracts.
patterns: Logical-property migration: codemod margin-left/right/top/bottom to inline/block equivalents repo-wide; lint blocks new physical properties.
RTL smoke page: one page rendering nav, forms, tables, and icons under dir=rtl, screenshotted per release against the mirror list.
useCases: Products launching Arabic/Hebrew/Urdu markets.
Global products keeping one responsive system across 20+ locales.
Audit: hardcoded margin-left, non-mirroring arrows, buttons that explode with German labels.
antiPatterns: Physical-direction CSS: margin-left sprinkled through codebase, making RTL a rewrite instead of an attribute
Row-reverse band-aids: 'fixing' RTL by reversing flex instead of trusting dir
Fixed-width labels: buttons sized for English that shatter with translated strings
Everything-mirrors: flipping logos, clocks, and playback controls that read wrong mirrored

accessibility.notes: Correct dir attributes are an accessibility requirement (WCAG 1.3.2 meaningful sequence; H58 dir usage): screen readers switch reading behavior with dir - wrong direction is wrong narration; DOM order must remain logical in both directions.
accessibility.fallback: If full RTL support cannot ship for a locale, disable that locale's UI (content-only mode) rather than shipping a broken mirrored interface.

skills.name: Responsive Testing & QA
skills.summary: The verification layer: viewport test matrix, visual regression, real-device checks, and zoom/RTL/locale passes that prove layouts work.

sections.definition: Responsive testing is the discipline that keeps every other layout skill honest: a defined viewport/device matrix, automated visual regression at each width, manual passes for zoom (200%/400%), RTL, and long-locale strings, and real-device spot checks for touch behaviors. Layout quality claims ('it's responsive') are replaced by evidence: which widths, which locales, and which zoom levels passed, and when.
principles: A written viewport matrix, not vibes: the tier widths (320/640/768/1024/1280/1536) plus 200%/400% zoom are the documented pass set.
Visual regression automates the matrix: screenshot diffs at every tier width on every PR catch the overflow nobody eyeballed.
Zoom IS a responsive test: 400% zoom on a 1280px laptop renders a 320px effective width - low-vision users live in your mobile tier (WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10).
Locale passes are layout passes: German (35% longer), Arabic (RTL), and Japanese (CJK line rules) are the minimum string-stress set.
Real devices verify what emulators cannot: touch targets, safe areas, scroll physics, and OS-level font scaling (iOS/Android accessibility sizes).
Test content, not lorem ipsum: longest real strings, empty states, and worst-case data volumes are the fixtures that find overflow.
Findings are tickets with a width attached: 'broken at 768px with German copy' - reproducible beats 'looks weird sometimes'.

tokens.notes: Zoom passes included in the matrix (1.4.4/1.4.10)
Overflow fixtures: longest label, empty state, max rows
Screenshot diff gate on every pull request
iOS/Android spot checks: targets, safe areas, OS font scale
dir=rtl page render vs the mirror list
OS-level text scaling verified on devices
Bugs cite width, locale, and screenshot

composition: Composes with breakpoints-strategy and fluid-container-queries: the tier set and slot list define exactly which widths and containers the matrix covers.
Composes with sibling layout guides: every layout pattern ships with its test slot (sidebar/main/modal) registered in the matrix.
Composes with zoom-reflow (skill-accessibility guide 11): the zoom and reflow passes are shared contracts between both repos.
patterns: Matrix-as-config: the viewport/locale/zoom matrix lives in a config file consumed by the visual-regression tool - tests and docs stay in sync.
Overflow canary: an automated probe walks pages at each width and fails on horizontal scroll of reading content or clipped interactive elements.
useCases: Design systems gating component releases on the full matrix.
i18n product launches: locale stress passes before market open.
Ongoing QA: regression gates keeping responsive debt from accumulating.
antiPatterns: Two-width testing: signing off at 375px and 1440px while the 768-1024 middle tier rots
Lorem ipsum QA: placeholder strings that never overflow, hiding the German-label explosion
Emulator-only trust: declaring touch and safe-area work without ever holding a device
Ungated regressions: visual diffs run manually, after the overflow already shipped

accessibility.notes: Zoom and OS-font-scale passes are accessibility conformance tests (WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10), not polish: low-vision users browse at widths your matrix must include - the 400% zoom pass IS a responsive test.
accessibility.fallback: If the full matrix cannot run before release, run the subset in priority order: 320px, 400% zoom, RTL locale, then widest - and ship the remainder as documented known issues with owners.
